note: Multi-hop questions that cannot be answered without carrying a reading across steps. Ground truth comes from the DashboardQA dataset, NOT from our own inspection of a live capture - so it can rot exactly like eval/questions.json, and additionally may not match how these particular workbooks render today. Dashboard URLs are kept verbatim in the dataset's browse form; eval.js rewrites them to the embed form at run time. Every entry started scored:false; the human checkpoint on 2026-08-10 reviewed the agent's real answers against the dataset's expected_answer BEFORE any expect value was written (see docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-discoveries-memory.md Task 10) and flipped all four to scored:true. For crsi-pledges-metro-vs-regional and cities-rental-fluctuation the agent's live answer disagreed with the dataset - in both cases the human chose to trust the dataset rather than independently re-verify the live dashboard, so those two entries score the agent as wrong on a policy call, not a confirmed-correct ground truth. Separately: crsi-pledges-metro-vs-regional's {not} requirement has never been exercised live against a genuine wrong-but-present answer (every observed live run of this question either matched the agent's over-inclusive TAS answer or errored to an empty string, which fails matchesExpect before {not} is ever evaluated) - {not} is proven only by evalMatch.test.js's unit tests, not by a live run of this file.
